analysis:
Examined ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift head lines 1380-2230. The only change visible in these units is the addition of two optional operations at head lines 1518-1525. stopsAsked defaults to returning nil. serveUnlessStopped defaults to nil, meaning plain serve is used. Per its doc comment, serveUnlessStopped is checked on the leading Mac under the start lock, so a stop that took the lock first is never undone.

This is a local onboarding/UI race fix: a stop asked during a start should not be overridden by that start's serve. It is not an authorization or crypto boundary. No coordinator, attestation (TB-009/TB-011), encryption (A-001) or cache (T-041) behavior changes here.

The defaults preserve prior behavior. Older builds return a nil count, so the TOCTOU guard is skipped and plain serve runs. This is an availability nuance (A-018), not a security regression.

Unchanged surrounding code was reviewed:
- shownName (line 2063) sanitizes names to at most 40 characters with no control characters.
- runAsAdministrator runs the owner-only link script with sudo; this relates to the TB-014/T-062 style admin prompt but is unchanged.
- localNetwork waiting is unchanged.

For integration, the following need checking in other batches:
- Head ranges 2852-3539, which use stopsBefore and serveUnlessStopped.
- The live OnboardingLive implementation, to confirm the stopsAsked counter in ClusterSetupRecord is read and compared under the same lock that stop takes.
- Whether a nil count, from an older peer build, can resurrect serving after a stop on either Mac; this would be an availability/consent issue, not confidentiality.

No findings from this batch.
